scope: large (increment A of three; B1/B2/C stay in proposal.md, out of scope for this PR)
inspiration: crackmes.one 6a3822888a86e4c2c55254fe selam.exe 0x140002d50: 1267 lines, 159 declarations, 63 synthetic return-address stores, BCrypt arguments as stack blobs
gating_rationale: It REMOVES CODE (the fall-through past the interrupt) and is transform-tier, so it ships behind a named option per CLAUDE.md. Default-on because the acceptance command carries no --option and because the evidence bar is met: 0/675 datatest assertions move, it is 20.5% faster on the witness, and it is gated on the Windows compiler spec plus the exact lifted `swi(0x29:1)` shape, so it is structurally inert everywhere else.
decisions: The filed hypothesis -- C++ small-string-object type recovery plus stack-variable splitting -- is REFUTED. The function constructs no std::string at all (no MSVC SSO signature `_Myres=0xf` at +0x18 anywhere in 0x140002d50..0x140004550; the nearest string object is in the caller at 0x140004a95), so no amount of STL layout recovery would fire here. See docs/features/large-function-malformed-output/proposal.md sec 5.

The real cause is an unmodelled instruction: x86 SLEIGH lifts `INT imm8` to `intloc = swi(imm8); call [intloc]` (ia.sinc:3671), a `call` with no matching push, and x86-64-win.cspec's __fastcall carries extrapop=8 stackshift=8. Every interrupt therefore raises RSP by 8 and the frame degenerates where the paths join.

The four filed complaints are THREE independent defects, not one. The 'impossible condition' v13 != v13 + 6 is faithful (MSVC really emitted LEA RAX,[R12+6]; CMP R12,RAX; JZ at 0x14000385a) and belongs to a REP STOSB recovery gap; it survives this fix, which is why the captain kept it off this acceptance.

The acceptance was RE-CUT by the captain on this evidence: `stdout_matches: [std::string]` is unsatisfiable soundly on this witness. The replacement pair (return-address store absent, BCrypt call by value present) was verified in both directions before any engine code was written, via `--assert 'flow <a> callreturn'` on the eleven int 0x29 sites and independently via a byte-patched image.

The alternative fix -- do not apply extrapop to a `call` whose instruction never pushed -- is strictly more general (it also covers INT1/INT3/INTO and int 0x80) and needs no Windows gate, but it changes the stack solver for every architecture and every call in the corpus. INT3 genuinely does return, so the two are not interchangeable. Left for its own proposal.

No 'Subroutine does not return' warning is buffered at the plant, unlike the named-no-return path. The divergence is definitional rather than a surprise, and the witness holds eleven sites in one function whose complaint is noise.

acceptance.promotion_note: The recorded target is dataset-only, so promote() refused to vendor it. tests/cli/ carries BOTH clauses verbatim against a synthesized 1,536-byte PE32+ (decompiler/crates/kuna-analysis/tests/fixtures/fastfail_x86_64.exe, regenerated by fastfail_x86_64.py) that reproduces the same shape: `--option fastfailnoreturn off` gives `char *v3; // rsp`, `*(unsigned long long *)&v3[-8] = 0x14000103d;` and `BCryptGenerateSymmetricKey(*(unsigned long long *)&v3[0x38],...)`; the default gives `BCryptGenerateSymmetricKey(v3,v1,v2,0x20)`.

stage_test.passes: two-pass: pass 1 `option fastfailnoreturn off` (the bug), pass 2 default (the fix)
stage_test.note: A 31-byte x86-64 Windows bytechunk: sub rsp,0x28 / spill rcx / test / jne past / mov ecx,5 / int 0x29 / reload the local / ret. Off: `char *vN; // rsp` and `*(unsigned long long *)&vN[0x20]`. Default: `return a0;`. No SSA index is pinned.

mechanism_note: Proved three ways before and after implementing. (1) `--assert 'flow <a> callreturn'` on the eleven int 0x29 sites of the witness: 1267 -> 1171 lines, 63 -> 0 return-address stores. (2) Byte-patching the 30 `MOV ECX,5 ; INT 0x29` sites to NOPs: 1121 lines, 0 stores. (3) The shipped option: 1267 -> 1147 lines, 63 -> 0 stores, 160 -> 149 declarations, and BCryptGenerateSymmetricKey(v52,&v55,v62,v54).

regression_sweep.method: whole-binary `kuna decompile-all` before/after (--option fastfailnoreturn off vs default) on one release build, diffed per function and classified by normalized statement shape
regression_sweep.note: All five are Windows PEs, since the option is inert on every other image by construction. Non-Windows coverage is the 675-assertion datatest corpus and the 631-assertion stages corpus, both byte-identical.

changed.classification: every changed function shrinks; the removed shapes are the defect's own signature (86 return-address stores, 13 `v = &v[8]` stack bumps, 9 `char *v; // rsp`, 6 `v = &Stack0000000000000000`), and every added shape is a pre-existing statement re-emitted after SSA renumbering or a re-associated comparison. Not one named call is lost; three appear (a stack argument becomes recoverable).
improvement only; the call-name set is identical, six more call sites

one function, sub_45032a, in a garbage-decode region: an 80-line block that used the interrupt's RETURN VALUE (`v7 = (*(code *)swi(0x29))();`) collapses to six honest lines. The seven lost 'calls' are all CONCAT/LOCK/UNLOCK pseudo-calls inside it; no named function call disappears anywhere in the image.

speed_note: Faster, not slower: cutting flow at the interrupt decodes strictly less. Measured with scripts.pipeline.timeit (warmup + median of 7) on the witness function.
out_of_scope: B1 -- fold INT_NOTEQUAL(V, INT_ADD(V, #c)) to false for c != 0. Removes the `v13 != v13 + 6` text the need quotes. Sound over modular arithmetic; ~40 lines in p3_dataflow.
B2 -- extend memsetrecover to the REP STOSB / REP MOVSB loop shape. 21 sites in the witness, ~105 lines and ~21 induction variables.
C -- a libcsigs-shaped Win32 signature table (bcrypt/kernel32/advapi32). Names resolve from the import table today; arities do not.
